# `nish/net/tls/record`

The TLS 1.3 record layer (RFC 8446 §5): the framing of a byte stream into records, the protection of one direction of it under a traffic secret, and the next secret a KeyUpdate moves to.

```ts
import {
  TLS_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC,
  TLS_ALERT_CLOSE_NOTIFY,
  TLS_ALERT_LEVEL_FATAL,
  TLS_ALERT_LEVEL_WARNING,
  TLS_ALERT_RECORD_OVERFLOW,
  TLS_ALERT_USER_CANCELED,
  TLS_CONTENT_ALERT,
  TLS_CONTENT_APPLICATION_DATA,
  TLS_CONTENT_CHANGE_CIPHER_SPEC,
  TLS_CONTENT_HANDSHAKE,
  TLS_HANDSHAKE_KEY_UPDATE,
  TLS_KEY_UPDATE_RECORDS,
  TLS_LAST_SEQUENCE,
  TLS_MAX_CIPHERTEXT,
  TLS_MAX_PLAINTEXT,
  TLS_MAX_RECORD,
  TLS_RECORD_HEADER_SIZE,
  TLS_RECORD_TAG_SIZE,
  TlsRecordProtection,
  TlsRecordReader,
  tlsNextTrafficSecret,
  tlsRecordLength,
  tlsRecordWindowFits,
} from "nish/net/tls/record";
```

```ts
import { TlsRecordProtection, TlsRecordReader } from "nish/net/tls/record";

const write = new TlsRecordProtection();
write.install(TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, serverApplicationSecret);
const n: i32 = write.seal(TLS_CONTENT_APPLICATION_DATA, data, 0, len, 0, out, at);
```

<scalar-detail title="Framing">

A record is a five-byte header — the content type, a legacy
version and a 16-bit length — and that many bytes. `TlsRecordReader` holds
the bytes of a stream that are not yet a whole record, in a buffer big
enough for the largest record the RFC allows (2^14 + 256 bytes of body),
borrowed from a `BufferPool` only while it holds any, and says as soon as
a header is in whether the record is one this layer will read: a content
type it does not know is `unexpected_message`, and a length past the limit
is `record_overflow`, before any of the body is waited for. The legacy
version is ignored, as §5.1 says it must be.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Protection">

`TlsRecordProtection` is one direction of a connection:
cleartext until `install` gives it a suite and a traffic secret, then
TLSCiphertext (§5.2) under the AEAD the suite names. Each record's nonce is
the traffic IV XORed with the 64-bit record sequence number (§5.3), and its
additional data is the record's own header. Inside, the content is followed
by its real type and by zero padding (§5.4); `open` finds the type by
reading every byte of the decrypted record whatever the padding is, so how
much padding there was is not in its timing, and refuses a record that is
padding and nothing else. Both `seal` and `open` write into a buffer the
caller owns and answer a count, and what they allocate on the way dies with
the call (docs/LANGUAGE.md, "Memory model"), so a connection that has
finished its handshake moves records without moving the arena.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Refusals are alerts.** Every function that can refuse answers the alert to
send, negated, as a negative count: `-TLS_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC` for a record
that does not authenticate, `-TLS_ALERT_RECORD_OVERFLOW` for one past the
limits, `-TLS_ALERT_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE` for a type that cannot be here, and
`-TLS_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR` for a mistake of the caller's — a window outside
its array, an output too small, content over 2^14 bytes. Nothing the peer
sends can make it panic.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

A traffic secret arrives as plain bytes, since that is how
`nish/net/tls` hands it over. The key, the IV and the AES key schedule
derived from it are held in the protection's fields, because a `Secret` may
not be one (NL2430), in arrays the protection reuses for every key it is
given, and are zeroed when it is installed again or cleared — the key and
IV with `secureZero`, the schedule with `aesKeyWipe`, the volatile `wipe`
of its round keys (the kernels' powers of H included) and of H. The key and
IV are derived straight into place, in an HKDF scratch that is wiped after
each derivation, and the schedule is expanded into place by `aesKeyInto`
(TLS-2 in `docs/security/tls.md`). A caller that holds the traffic secret
as a `Secret` installs it with `installHeld` and ratchets it in place with
`advanceHeld`, so the secret itself is never plain outside `exposeWith`.

</scalar-detail>

The record layer is sans-IO: `nish/net/tls/record-server` runs it over a
stream for `TlsServer`, and `nish/net/tls-tcp` puts that on a socket.
Written from RFC 8446 §5, not ported from another implementation.

## tlsNextTrafficSecret

The traffic secret a KeyUpdate moves one direction to (RFC 8446 §7.2):
`HKDF-Expand-Label(secret, "traffic upd", "", Hash.length)` over the hash
`hashLength` names, held as a `Secret`. The old secret is the caller's to
wipe.

```ts
function tlsNextTrafficSecret(
  hashLength: i32,
  trafficSecret: Secret<u8[]>,
): Secret<u8[]>
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hashLength" type="i32" required>

The hash length of the connection's suite, 32 or 48, and so how many bytes are derived.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="trafficSecret" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The direction's current traffic secret. This function does not wipe it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;">

A fresh `Secret` holding the next traffic secret, which the caller owns and wipes.

</scalar-field>

## tlsRecordLength

The length of the record whose header starts at `buf[off]`, header
included, read from the `avail` bytes there: 0 while fewer than five are
in, or the alert negated when the header announces a type this layer does
not know (`unexpected_message`) or a body past 2^14 + 256 bytes
(`record_overflow`, §5.2). The legacy version is not read (§5.1).

```ts
function tlsRecordLength(
  buf: u8[],
  off: i32,
  avail: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the bytes received so far.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where in `buf` the record's header starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="avail" type="i32" required>

How many bytes, from `off`, have arrived.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The whole record's length in bytes, header included; 0 while the header is not all in;
    `-TLS_ALERT_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE` or `-TLS_ALERT_RECORD_OVERFLOW` for a header this layer refuses;
    `-TLS_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR` when `buf[off .. off + avail)` is not inside `buf`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsRecordWindowFits

Whether `[off, off + len)` is a window inside an array of `length` elements: every caller's range check.
It is written as `off <= length - len`, not `off + len <= length`, so a large `off` cannot overflow.

```ts
function tlsRecordWindowFits(
  length: i32,
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many elements the array has.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the window starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many elements the window spans.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when `off` and `len` are not negative and the window ends at or before `length`.

</scalar-field>

## TlsRecordProtection

One direction of a connection's record protection. Cleartext (`suite` 0)
until `install`; then every record is sealed or opened under the suite's
AEAD with the key and IV of the traffic secret it was given, and its
sequence number counts from 0. `contentType` is the type the last `open`
found inside a protected record, or the header's type for a cleartext one.

Every array it fills is made by the constructor: a key of each length, an
AES key schedule of each size, the IV, the next traffic secret of each
hash, and the HKDF scratch the keys are derived in. `key` and `aes` point
at the ones the installed suite uses, so changing suites allocates nothing.

```ts
class TlsRecordProtection
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsRecordProtection()` | Makes a cleartext direction and every array it will fill, so that no install allocates. The record limit starts at `TLS_KEY_UPDATE_RECORDS`. |
| `aes: AesKey \| null` | The AES key schedule for the two AES-GCM suites, the one of the installed key's size. |
| `aes128: AesKey` |  |
| `aes256: AesKey` |  |
| `contentType: i32` | The real content type of the last record `open` answered. |
| `iv: u8[]` | The 12-byte traffic IV (§7.3), zeroed while the direction is cleartext. |
| `key: u8[]` | The AEAD key (§7.3): the suite's key length, zeroed while the direction is cleartext. |
| `key16: u8[]` | The arrays `key` and `aes` point into: AES-128's and ChaCha20's or AES-256's. |
| `key32: u8[]` |  |
| `next: u8[]` | Where `advance` derives the next traffic secret: HashLen bytes of it. |
| `recordLimit: i64` | The sequence number at which a writer moves to the next key. Readable and writable, so a test can bring the key update forward; a reader ignores it. |
| `sequence: i64` | The next record's sequence number (§5.3). |
| `advance(secret: u8[]): boolean` | Moves this direction to the next traffic secret (§7.2), the KeyUpdate step: `secret`, the current one, is overwritten in place by the next, and the keys are installed from it; the next secret's own copy is wiped. The next secret is derived in place inside an arena block, as `derive`'s keys are. False, as `install` answers, when the keys do not install. |
| `advanceHeld(secret: Secret<u8[]>): boolean` | `advance` on a traffic secret the caller holds as a `Secret`: the next traffic secret (§7.2) is written over `secret`'s bytes in place, a ratchet that leaves no copy of either, and the keys are installed from it with `installHeld`. False, as `advance` answers, when the keys do not install; a secret that is not its hash's length is left as it was. |
| `install(suite: i32, secret: u8[]): boolean` | Protects this direction under `secret` from the next record on: the suite's key and IV (§7.3), the sequence number back to 0, and what this replaces zeroed by `clear`. `false`, leaving the direction cleartext, for a suite `nish/net/tls/schedule` does not know or a secret that is not its hash's length.<br><br>The key, the IV and the AES key schedule are written into the arrays this direction made when it was constructed, so an install allocates nothing that outlives it (TLS-3). |
| `installHeld(suite: i32, secret: Secret<u8[]>): boolean` | `install` from a traffic secret the caller holds as a `Secret`: the key and IV are derived from it straight into this direction's arrays, the plain output of each derivation wiped, and the AES key schedule expanded into place inside an arena block, as `derive`'s is. `false`, leaving the direction cleartext, where `install` answers it. |
| `isProtected(): boolean` | Whether records in this direction are protected. |
| `nonceInto(nonce: u8[]): void` | The per-record nonce (§5.3): the IV with the sequence number XORed into its last eight bytes, big-endian. |
| `open(record: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, out: u8[], at: i32): i32` | Reads the whole record `record[off .. off + len)`, header included, and writes its content at `out[at]`: answers the content's length and sets `contentType`. Cleartext, the content is the body and the type the header's: `application_data` is `unexpected_message`, since it is never sent in the clear, and a body over 2^14 bytes is `record_overflow`. Protected, the header's type must be `application_data` (`unexpected_message` otherwise), the body must authenticate under this record's nonce with the header as additional data (`bad_record_mac`), the decrypted record may be no longer than 2^14 + 1 bytes (`record_overflow`), and its last non-zero byte is the real type — one that is all zeros is `unexpected_message` (§5.4). Every refusal is the alert negated; a window outside `record`, a `len` that is not the header's, or too little room at `out[at]` is `-TLS_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR`.<br><br>A protected record that fails to authenticate leaves the sequence number where it was; one that authenticates spends its number even when its content is then refused. |
| `seal(type: i32, data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, padding: i32, out: u8[], at: i32): i32` | Writes one record of content type `type` holding `data[off .. off + len)` at `out[at]` and answers its length, header included. Cleartext, it is a TLSPlaintext, `padding` must be 0 and `type` may not be `application_data`; protected, it is a TLSCiphertext whose inner plaintext carries `type` and then `padding` zero bytes (§5.4), and the sequence number moves on. `-TLS_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR`, with nothing written, for content over 2^14 bytes, a padding that would take the inner plaintext past 2^14 + 1, a window outside `data`, too little room at `out[at]`, or a sequence number that would wrap. |

## TlsRecordReader

The bytes of a stream that are not yet a whole record. The buffer is
`TLS_MAX_RECORD` bytes, borrowed from `pool` by the first `push` that brings
a byte, kept between records, and given back, zeroed with `giveSecret`, by
`reset`, as its connection ends: a reader that has not been pushed to since
holds no buffer at all. `push` takes what fits, and the
bytes of a record stay until `consume` lets them go. The caller reads
`buffer[start .. start + next())` for the record, while `next()` is above 0.

A reader starts with a pool of its own, one buffer deep; `borrowFrom` points
it at a pool a server shares between its slots.

```ts
class TlsRecordReader
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsRecordReader()` | Makes an empty reader with a pool of its own, one buffer deep. No buffer is taken until the first `push` brings a byte. |
| `buffer: u8[]` | The bytes held, or `empty` while the reader holds none. |
| `end: i32` | One past the last byte pushed. |
| `start: i32` | The first byte not yet consumed. |
| `consume(n: i32): void` | Lets the first `n` held bytes go: the record `next` answered, once it is handled. When none are left the next record starts at the front; the buffer stays until `reset`. |
| `next(): i32` | The length of the whole record at `start`, header included, once every byte of it is in; 0 before; or the alert negated for a header this layer refuses, as `tlsRecordLength` says. |
| `push(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Copies as many of `data[off .. off + len)` as fit and answers how many, after moving what is held to the front. A window outside `data` is `-TLS_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR`, and nothing is copied. |
| `reset(): void` | Forgets every byte, for a connection that starts again in the same slot, and gives the buffer back. |
| `space(): i32` | How many bytes `push` would take now. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="16,640" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_MAX_CIPHERTEXT: i32`

The longest body a protected record may have: 2^14 + 256 bytes (§5.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16,384" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_MAX_PLAINTEXT: i32`

The most content one record carries: 2^14 bytes (§5.1).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16,645" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_MAX_RECORD: i32`

The longest whole record, header included.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="20" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC: i32`

`bad_record_mac`: a protected record did not authenticate.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_CLOSE_NOTIFY: i32`

`close_notify` (§6.1): the sender writes nothing more.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_LEVEL_FATAL: i32`

An alert's level byte for every error alert.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_LEVEL_WARNING: i32`

An alert's level byte for `close_notify` and `user_canceled`. TLS 1.3 reads nothing into it (§6).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_RECORD_OVERFLOW: i32`

`record_overflow`: a record longer than the limits allow.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="90" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_ALERT_USER_CANCELED: i32`

`user_canceled` (§6.1): a warning that the peer is abandoning the handshake; a close follows.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="21" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CONTENT_ALERT: i32`

`alert` (§6): a level and a description.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="23" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CONTENT_APPLICATION_DATA: i32`

`application_data`, and the outer type of every protected record.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="20" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CONTENT_CHANGE_CIPHER_SPEC: i32`

`change_cipher_spec`: the compatibility record of RFC 8446 §D.4, one byte of 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="22" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_CONTENT_HANDSHAKE: i32`

`handshake` (§4).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="24" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_HANDSHAKE_KEY_UPDATE: i32`

The KeyUpdate handshake message (§4.6.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16,777,216" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_KEY_UPDATE_RECORDS: i64`

How many records one key protects before a writer moves to the next with a
KeyUpdate: 2^24. AES-GCM's limit is 2^24.5 full-size records per key (RFC
8446 §5.5), and this is under it with room; ChaCha20-Poly1305's is far past
it, and one rule for all three suites keeps the writer simple.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9,007,199,254,740,991" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_LAST_SEQUENCE: i64`

The sequence number no record is sealed or opened at: 2^53 − 1. The counter
must never wrap (§5.3), and stopping here, at a number no connection
reaches, keeps the `i64` it is held in far from its own overflow.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_RECORD_HEADER_SIZE: i32`

The bytes before a record's body: its type, a legacy version and a 16-bit length.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_RECORD_TAG_SIZE: i32`

The AEAD tag every protected record ends with; all three suites' is 16 bytes.

</scalar-card>
